headline: Highest risk is medium: Authelia can broker auth to Taipy, creating default-pathway leakage and trust/conflict issues, but no direct shared workspace or documented pairwise exploit is shown.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented between authelia and taipy. Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, while taipy shows no I/O surfaces or browser/subprocess behavior, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or message queue is added between authelia and taipy, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not route untrusted text from one agent into the other's instruction channel.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/ForwardAuth, so it can move identity-related data outward; taipy has no documented egress and no data classes touched. The pair lacks a shared workspace or sensitive-data evidence, so leakage is possible only through explicit integration, not by default.
conditions: IF authelia is configured to forward identity claims or headers containing sensitive data to taipy-backed workflows, leakage risk increases.
IF both agents are placed on the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict forwarded claims to the minimum required set.
Disable any shared workspace mounts between the agents.
Review logs for identity headers before enabling integration.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction on forwarded auth data.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls, while taipy shows no write, network, or concurrency surface in the profile. Because overlapping mutable-resource access is not documented, a direct capability conflict is not established; uncertainty stays low rather than none because taipy's concurrency model is empty.
conditions: IF taipy is deployed with write access to the same external resource Authelia protects, conflicts become plausible.
IF both agents are granted overlapping OAuth scopes on one backend, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid granting both agents write access to the same backend.
Document ownership of each mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can act as an auth gate and taipy is a scheduler/automation tool, so taipy may consume auth-derived outputs as inputs in a default integration. Without a verification step documented, downstream actions could be triggered by incorrect auth decisions or claims, making cascading error plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF taipy consumes Authelia-produced claims or headers without validation, cascading error becomes active.
IF taipy triggers scheduled actions based on auth state, incorrect upstream decisions can propagate.
mitigations: Add a validation step before taipy acts on auth-derived data.
Log and review the exact claims forwarded from Authelia.
Use allowlists for accepted identity attributes.
requires-engineering: add explicit schema validation between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no PHI, residency, or retention commitments, so no concrete compliance breach is evidenced. The only plausible issue is policy mismatch if Authelia forwards identity data into taipy workflows under stricter local rules, which is a limited, configuration-dependent concern.
conditions: IF regulated identity data is routed through Authelia into taipy logs or exports, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not present in either agent, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm whether regulated data is in scope before integration.
Set retention limits on any shared logs.
requires-engineering: implement residency and deletion controls if regulated data is introduced.
